The common fixed point and μ are exact (g·N·g⁻¹ = μ·N over K, for the nilpotent part N of the parabolic), and so are μ⁴ ≠ 1 and μ⁶ ≠ 1. The parabolics (g1²·g2)ⁿ·(g1²·g2·g1·g2·g1·g2⁻¹·g1⁻³·g2⁻¹·g1⁻¹)·(g1²·g2)⁻ⁿ translate by μⁿτ, which shrinks to 0 as n → +∞: non-trivial elements converging to the identity, so the group is not discrete.

A finite order m would make e^{iθ} a primitive m-th root of unity of degree ≤ 2 over ℚ(tr²/det), so φ(m) ≤ 6; no such m has (g1²·g2)ᵐ = 1 (checked exactly). g1²·g2 has infinite order. Its powers rotate by multiples of θ, which are dense in the circle and accumulate at the identity: the group is not discrete.
